message:
fix(android): the phone asks where observations go, and 409 is not "PC is off"

The phone derived the observe port as http + 1, always. Behind TLS on 443
that is 444: nothing answers, the observation never lands, and the connect
goes ahead with the directory holding no address for this phone. What the
user sees is a connection that does not work, which reads like the PC being
off rather than a server that needs one setting.

Same rule as the native client, from the same vectors: the advertised port
wins, http keeps its documented +1, https with no advertisement refuses and
says why, 65535 has nowhere to add one. The metadata rides on the login
response; a phone that reopens on a stored session never sees one, so that
path asks /healthz, which needs no session.

Reached and said-nothing are kept apart there. Both used to arrive as an
empty endpoint, and on https both would then have been reported as a
missing server setting -- sending whoever read it to configure a server
that was simply down.

The advertised host is validated here because the server does not validate
it: it is stored as whatever the operator typed. A value with a scheme, a
path, a port or a space is not a host name, and rejecting one does not
discard the port that came with it.

409 was mapped to "the host is offline" for every case. The directory now
also answers 409 when it has no address observation for this client, which
is a different thing and one the phone can repair. So DirectoryException
carries the status and the server's error name, the message for that case
says what is actually happening, and the connect re-observes once and
retries once -- only on that error, never in a loop, and without signing
out, because nothing is wrong with the session.

The log uploader had its own idea of what a url is: startsWith("http"),
which is true of "https://" and also of "httpx://", and anything else got
http:// prepended here. It now asks DirectoryClient for the same answer the
rest of the app uses. A session token goes out in a header on that request;
which scheme carries it is not a question two files should answer
separately.

The unit tests needed the real org.json. The stub in android.jar throws on
every call unless returnDefaultValues is set, and setting it would make
JSONObject hand back nulls and zeros -- a parser test that passes while
parsing nothing. Nothing about that dependency ships in the APK.

Untouched deliberately: UpdateFlow and UpdateManifest stay https-only, and
the cleartext policy is not widened.
